predecessors.name: Jinhan confederacy
predecessors.text: the Jinhan confederacy's land: Silla 'began as Saro-guk, a statelet within the 12-member confederacy known as Jinhan'

successors.name: Unified Silla
successors.text: Silla after the conquest of Baekje and of the land south of the Taedong River

ledger.x: 378: Silla appears on the map, replacing the Jinhan outline.
468: Goguryeo takes the Gangwon edge of Silla.
551 at the latest: Silla is back on its northern frontier.
551: Silla's share of the Han River conquest.
553: Silla takes the whole Han River region from Baekje.

553: the Han River fighting ends with Silla in possession ('launched an attack on the Han River valley during the year 553'); Baekje's counterattack and King Seong's death in 554 are a separate episode.
671: Silla expels the Tang from Baekje.
676: Silla holds the peninsula south of the Taedong.
681: the Silla dossier ends; Tamna's tribute continues in the Unified Silla dossier (to 925, Tamna infobox).

wars.name: Conquest of Gaya
wars.outcome: Silla destroyed Takgitan Gaya (529), took Geumgwan Gaya (532) and Daegaya (562); the confederacy ended.

wars.name: Silla-Baekje campaign for the Han River valley
wars.outcome: Silla and Baekje took the valley from Goguryeo in 551; Silla took Baekje's half in late 553 and killed King Seong in 554.

wars.name: Silla-Tang conquest of Baekje
wars.outcome: Baekje ended in 660; Silla and Tang divided the occupation.

wars.name: Silla-Tang War
wars.outcome: Silla victory: Tang left Baekje (671) and the land south of the Taedong (676); Tang recognised Silla's sovereignty there in 736.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary; every frontier (Baekje, Goguryeo, Gaya, Tang-held Baekje) is approximate, and the east-coast extension to 40.1 N from 554 is unverified.
The line 'from the mouth of the Taedong River in the west to the East Korea Bay' is a described limit, not a surveyed one.
